thread:
alex.k: Heads-up — deploy-bot flagged a p95 latency regression on canary for eu-dedicated. Suggest evaluating fastpath rollback and pinning the pool. :eyes:
jamie: Can you paste the alert payload? how big is the regression?
deploy-bot: ALERT: canary/eu-dedicated p95 increased 350ms -> 980ms (baseline 320ms). Threshold=+250ms. Samples: 1200 requests in last 10m. EventID=evt_6600001.
maria: Ugh. That's above our rollback threshold (>=+200ms sustained 5m). Recommend hold traffic, pin current version on dedicated, and notify SRE.
tyler: Agree on hold. Any consumer-facing errors?
alex.k: No 5xx spikes reported, mostly latency. Customer impact risk moderate (embeddings jobs longer).
lina.prod: Prep a short customer blurb in case we need to escalate — keep it non-technical. I can draft if we decide to pin.
sre-oncall: I'm on it. Will run quick perf diff against last stable (v3.4.0) and attempt a targeted rollback to v3.4.0 on canary pool. Ping me when pin command is ready.
jamie: Proposed immediate actions:
- stop canary traffic: `deployctl traffic --pool eu-dedicated --set 0% --reason "latency regression"`
- pin pool to v3.4.0: `deployctl pin --pool eu-dedicated --version v3.4.0`
- run perf compare job `perfcmp --from v3.4.0 --to v3.4.1 --pool eu-dedicated`
- if perf diff < threshold, roll forward; else leave pinned and notify customers.
maria: I'll prepare the quick rollback runbook snippet for the oncall:
```
# rollback runbook (fastpath)
1) block new canary traffic
2) pin pool to previous stable
3) scale down new nodes gracefully
4) monitor p95, error-rate, and kv-cache hit-rate for 10m
5) if good, schedule controlled rollforward with canary slice
```
deploy-bot: ACTION: `traffic set` accepted. Old traffic: 10% -> New traffic: 0%. JobID=job_660000A.
alex.k: Thanks — @sre-oncall please execute the pin when ready. Lina, can you draft customer note? Keep it "We're investigating latency in EU; some requests may be slower".
lina.prod: Draft ready: "We observed slower response times in our EU inference pool. We've paused the canary rollout and reverted to the previous config to restore performance. We'll share an update within 60 minutes".
sre-oncall: Executing pin now: `deployctl pin --pool eu-dedicated --version v3.4.0`
deploy-bot: COMMAND: `deployctl pin --pool eu-dedicated --version v3.4.0` accepted. PinID=pin_660000X.
sre-oncall: Pin successfully applied. Monitoring metrics.
jamie: Running perf compare now. ETA ~3m.
jamie: perfcmp report: v3.4.0 p95=340ms, v3.4.1 p95=980ms. Delta +640ms. KV-cache warmup looks worse on v3.4.1.
maria: That's a clear regression. Keep pin for now, open follow-up ticket for model runtime team to investigate quantization change and KV behavior.
alex.k: I'll update release notes: mark v3.4.1 as reverted on eu-dedicated due to latency regression. Also flag rollback reason internally.
lina.prod: Sent customer note to the incident mailing list and posted a brief in #customer-status.
tyler: Any risk to other regions? Recommend scanning other pools for similar regressions before unpin.
sre-oncall: Running a quick sweep on usw2 and apac now. No similar spike observed in last 10m.
alex.k: OK keeping pin in place. Action items: 1) ticket to runtime w/ perf logs (maria) 2) release note update (alex.k) 3) customer follow-up if ETA >60m (lina.prod). Who owns the runtime ticket?
maria: I'll own it and tag the model-runtime team. Ticket created: RUNTIME-421. Included perf dump and steps to reproduce.
jamie: Documenting decision: manual rollback/pin executed due to sustained p95 regression > rollback threshold. No 5xx surge, no immediate customer-facing errors but latency impact unacceptable.
alex.k: Thanks everyone. I'll close thread after upstream confirms root cause next steps. :thumbsup:
